title: Open chest wound
summary: Call emergency services; leave exposed or use a clean nonocclusive dressing while monitoring breathing.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Open Chest Wounds
actions: Call emergency services immediately and use a safe position that makes breathing easiest unless reduced alertness or other injuries prevent it.
Leave the wound open to air or cover with a clean, dry, nonocclusive dressing. Use a purpose-made vented chest seal only if available and you know how.
If breathing worsens after a dressing is placed, loosen or remove it. Control bleeding around the wound without pressing on an embedded object.
Monitor breathing and alertness continuously. Start CPR and use an AED if breathing becomes absent or abnormal.
Keep the person warm and still; stabilize any embedded object with bulky dressings around it.
prohibitions: Do not seal the wound with unvented plastic.
Do not remove an embedded object.
Do not give food or drink.

emergencyCall.text: Every open or penetrating chest wound is a life-threatening emergency.
